method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited texts with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; the Regulations' Schedules 1-3 as tables (voca-schedules.l4), a seat-neutral core (voca-core.l4, with three regulative rules covering ss 29, 45, 46(10), 47, 47F, 47G and 47H-47K) and two seat layers (voca-seat.l4, voca-seat-funeral.l4) that restate no rule; no REFUSE (a Schedule 3 item that is not a leaf of the table answers `not covered`, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Victims of Crime Assistance Act 2006 (NT), reprint REPV014, as in force at 1 July 2025 (../../registers/source-bundle/Victims-of-Crime-Assistance-Act-2006-NT-current-reprint-REPV014.txt); with the Victims of Crime Assistance Regulations 2007 (NT), reprint REPV014R1, as in force at 25 March 2024 (subjects/au/nt/victims-of-crime-assistance-regulations-2007/registers/source-bundle/Victims-of-Crime-Assistance-Regulations-2007-NT-current-reprint-REPV014R1.txt); both unofficial copies from legislation.nt.gov.au

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run voca-schedules.l4 ; l4 run voca-core.l4 ; l4 run voca-seat.l4 ; l4 run voca-seat-funeral.l4 ; l4 run voca-cases-victim.l4 ; l4 run voca-cases-funeral.l4
checks.result: 245 assertions satisfied (209 in voca-cases-victim.l4, 36 in voca-cases-funeral.l4), 0 errors, 0 warnings (2026-10-24); 6 #TRACEs with an expect line (5 breaches: the Territory under ss 45, 29 and 47F, the person required to refund under ss 47 and 47G; 1 obligation pending: the Director's s 47K duty to reopen), each read and as expected
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: Act ss 4, 5, 6, 7 with regs 3-7 and 7A; ss 9-16 and 22 (primary, secondary, family and related victims and what each may apply for); ss 17-18 with reg 13 (exclusion where a Motor Accidents (Compensation) benefit or Return to Work compensation is paid or payable for the same injury, claimed or not; the other scheme's entitlement an input; counselling stays open); s 19 (death); ss 25, 25B, 26, 27(5), 28, 29 (interim payments, $5 000); ss 29A, 31, 37-43 (awards: s 38 $40 000 less interim, financial loss $10 000 less interim, the $7 500 standard-amount threshold; s 39 shared cap, proportional reduction and the s 39(5)-(7) witness priority; s 40 shared cap, dependants first, s 40(8)-(9); s 41 may reduce; s 42 must reduce by payments received; s 43 must not award); regs 14-16 with Schedules 1, 2 and 3 as tables, reg 18 (100%, 30%, 15%, no more), reg 19, regs 20-22, reg 23 (loss of earnings, NT AWE an input); ss 45-46 (payment, increase); s 47 (refund, a regulative rule on the recipient, at least 28 days, a debt to the Territory); ss 47A-47G (funeral expense assistance: within 2 years of death unless the Director accepts later; the lesser of reasonable cost net of other payments and $15 000; the s 47G refund); ss 47H-47K (closure if uncontactable); s 48 and Schedule 1 (NTCAT review; the NTCAT Act time limit an input); s 54 (no legal costs beyond reasonable disbursements). Out: Part 5 (recovery from offenders); s 61 and reg 26 (the levy, which falls on offenders, in revenue units whose value is not deposited); ss 21, 24, 33-36, 44, 55, 60, 62-70; regs 8-12, 24-25, 27-31. Read with subjects/au/nt/return-to-work-act-1986/ and subjects/au/nt/motor-accidents-compensation-act-1979/ (the s 17 and s 18 inputs) and subjects/au/social-security-act-1991/encodings/baseline-2026-10/ (s 17(2B): an award here is not compensation under the Social Security Act); cross-folder IMPORT is not possible.
seats: the victim applying for assistance (primary, secondary, family or related victim)
the person who paid for a victim's funeral
